findings.issue: sortRows indexes rows by the column key ('move', 'type', 'category'), but MoveRowData only has moveName/moveLabel/typeName/typeLabel/categoryName/categoryLabel (app/src/lib/queries.ts:54-83). Those three columns compare undefined vs undefined, return 0, and never reorder — while aria-sort still reports ascending/descent, so the spec's 'every column header is sortable' is broken and screen-reader users are told a sort happened. The acceptance test only checks aria-sort on the Move header, so it slipped through.
findings.suggestion: Map column key to a row value accessor (move→moveLabel, type→typeLabel, category→categoryLabel) or give MoveRowData fields named exactly like the column keys, and drop the 'as keyof MoveRowData' cast so TS catches mismatches.

findings.issue: The URL-sync effect bails out while a debounce timer is pending instead of cancelling it, so a Previous/Next page click made within ~250ms of typing leaves the timer armed; when it fires, navigateWith drops the page param and snaps the user back to page 1.
findings.suggestion: Clear the pending timer whenever params.q changes from outside (or on any URL change), e.g. clearTimeout(debounceTimer) at the top of the effect instead of returning early.

findings.issue: fetchJson throws on any non-404 response, but the app has no ErrorBoundary (app/src/app.tsx:28 wraps children only in Suspense), so an upstream 500/network failure becomes an unhandled rejection, a raw SSR error page, and an error on every client-side navigation to that route.
findings.suggestion: Add an ErrorBoundary (with a fallback page matching the site chrome) around the Suspense in app.tsx, and return a friendly error state (or a NotFound-style page) from the queries for fetch failures.

findings.issue: One 705-line module owns the API client, five module-scope promise caches, four derived indexes and all five pages' DTO builders; every route imports from it, making it the app's single point of evolution and review.
findings.suggestion: Split into lib/api.ts (fetchJson + cache), a small cache helper, and per-domain query modules (home/pokemon/move/ability/type) or at least per-resource builders.

findings.issue: The 'collect pokemon with id<=10000, resolve via directory, sort by id' loop is duplicated at queries.ts:358-368 (moves) and queries.ts:439-461 (abilities, with the hidden-flag wrinkle), and the English-effect fallback is duplicated at queries.ts:371-375 and 441-445.
findings.suggestion: Extract a collectDefaultForms(refs) helper and an englishShortEffectOrFlavor(record) helper next to format.ts and reuse them.

findings.issue: The same create-promise-or-reset-on-error cache boilerplate is repeated five times (lines 208-217, 224-230, 237-243, 251-259, 486-496), a maintenance hazard if eviction or TTL is ever needed.

Search input is bound with attr:value and then re-synced by hand through a ref and a lastUrlSearch mirror (index.tsx:30, 68-77), a non-idiomatic three-piece sync when a signal-driven value={searchText()} plus the debounce would be one mechanism.
findings.suggestion: Make searchText the single source of truth with value={searchText()}, and keep only the debounce → setParams direction plus a params→signal sync in the effect.

findings.issue: Despite the strict tsconfig, the raw API records in the pokemon-page builder are handled as 'any' throughout (also 548-549, 649-668), undercutting the otherwise-good DTO typing and hiding typos like the MoveTable one.
findings.suggestion: Declare minimal interfaces for the API payloads (species, pokemon, move, ability, type, evolution-chain) and let TS check the derivation code.

findings.issue: The head links /favicon.ico but app/public is empty, so every page load issues a 404.
findings.suggestion: Add a favicon to public/ or drop the link.

findings.issue: nitro is pinned to an exact beta (3.0.260610-beta) while v3 has since moved to RC builds (3.0.261029-rc), so the app won't pick up fixes and upgrades require an explicit bump.
findings.suggestion: Move to the current RC (or a caret range on the v3 RC channel) when bumping dependencies; document why the exact pin if reproducibility is the goal.

summary: A genuinely idiomatic SolidStart v2 app — documented query/"use server"/createAsync data loading, correct search-param semantics, clean server/client boundaries and consistent page structure — that I'd accept in a heartbeat structurally. It ships two real bugs the acceptance tests miss: Move/Type/Category column sorting is a silent no-op (column keys don't match row fields) while aria-sort claims otherwise, and a pending debounce timer can bounce a user off their pagination page. Add an ErrorBoundary and split the 705-line god data module, and this is a solid merge.
